articles.title: Turkiye’s Erdogan urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks
articles.summary: Turkish president hosts Zelenskyy in Istanbul as the two leaders agree to work on a new Black Sea grain corridor.
articles.body:
Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has urged both Russia and Ukraine to stop targeting civilian ships in the Black Sea , as he and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed to work on a new grain corridor through the waterway.

Erdogan made the comments on Saturday at a joint news conference with Zelenskyy in Istanbul, saying attacks on civilian vessels were unacceptable, whoever carries them out.

The talks came on the same day US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was growing international interest in a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea to secure grain and energy shipments by both countries.

“It is clear that attacks against civilian vessels and actions that further escalate tensions in the Black Sea serve no one’s interests,” Erdogan said.

“We cannot accept these attacks under any circumstances, regardless of who carries them out or what justification is offered,” he said, adding, “We call on all parties to act responsibly on this matter.”

Turkiye, which maintains ties with both Moscow and Kyiv, has been angered by the strikes on commercial shipping.

Ankara has sent Russia and Ukraine a proposal to end attacks, but says neither side has acted on it.

Zelenskyy accused Russia of making the situation in the Black Sea difficult and said a significant part of his conversation with Erdogan focused on security there.

“Today, I reached an agreement with President Erdogan to work on the Black Sea grain corridor,” he said.

He said Turkiye supports efforts to ensure safe navigation in the Black Sea and restore normal living conditions.

“We discussed with President Erdogan some ideas and proposals that can help,” Zelenskyy said, thanking the Turkish leader for the dialogue.

Erdogan said talks to restore safe navigation would continue.

“I believe that reaching an agreement on this issue would also give fresh impetus to efforts to secure lasting peace in Ukraine,” he said.

The US is reviewing proposals by Turkiye and India to get grain shipments moving, according to Rubio.

“This is threatening the world for food security and some energy security as well,” Rubio told a news conference in Atlanta, Georgia, following a G20 foreign ministers meeting. “We’d like to achieve it. It doesn’t solve the war, but at least it solves a unique aspect of it.”

Zelenskyy raises possibility of talks in Turkiye

Erdogan also welcomed renewed momentum behind efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war through diplomatic means, pointing in particular to US President Donald Trump’s initiative.

“At this point, we maintain that there can be no losers in a just peace,” he said, adding, “I would like to emphasise that we stand ready to make every possible effort to pave the way for peace”.

Turkiye has hosted several rounds of talks between Russia and Ukraine aimed at a lasting ceasefire and peace deal, which Erdogan said showed that “tangible results can be achieved through diplomacy”.

In a phone call with Trump on Wednesday, Erdogan said Turkiye was ready to support efforts to revive the diplomatic process and end the war, according to the Turkish president’s office.

Last week, the Kremlin said the next round of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US was planned to resume in November in the United Arab Emirates.

Zelenskyy said he had discussed that format with Erdogan, along with other options, including involving Turkiye, Europe and other partners, as well as the possibility of a meeting in Turkiye.

“Strong decisions are needed for there to be peace,” he said. “And it is necessary at all levels to send signals to Russia that there is no alternative to peace and that support for Ukraine will continue.”

articles.title: Bullied Ghana teenager shot to death on his way to school in Bronx: Mayor Mamdani says he spoke to Trump, Javits Frimpong's mother to get visa to see son for the last time
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has agreed to grant an immediate visa to the mother of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot while walking to school
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has agreed to grant an immediate visa to the mother of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot while walking to school in New York City's Bronx neighbourhood, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Saturday. Mamdani said he had spoken to Trump over the phone and the president had agreed to allow Frimpong's mother to travel to the US to say goodbye to her son in person.“The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away. Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately. All of New York City is mourning this tragedy,” Mamdani said in a statement.Frimpong was shot dead on Thursday morning while on his way to school in the Bronx. The 15-year-old was originally from Ghana and had moved to the US about a year ago to live with his father, who had hoped to give him a better life. Frimpong's father said he knew who was responsible for the shooting. He also said his son had been bullied at school and that those involved had recently been suspended.The suspects, three teenage boys wanted in connection with the shooting, remain at large, police said.The killing has shaken the local community, with religious leaders, family members and residents gathering at the spot where Frimpong collapsed after being shot. A vigil was held on Friday, with attendees praying for the Bronx and urging young people to stop the violence claiming lives in the neighbourhood.Among those attending was Leandra Feliz, the mother of Junior Guzman, a 15-year-old who was killed in 2018 in a case described as one of mistaken identity. Fourteen members of the Trinitarios gang slashed Guzman in the neck with machetes. He managed to reach the steps of St. Barnabas Hospital, where he died.Asked what message she had for Frimpong's family, Feliz said: “I'm only here to show support to the family because here we are again, another child of 15-years-old lost and I just want to be here to let the family know I'm here.”The New York City Department of Education expressed condolences to the family and school community, saying: “Our hearts are with this young person's family and school community during this unimaginably difficult time. We are making counseling and other supports are available to students, families, and staff who need them, and supporting NYPD as they investigate.”The police investigation into the fatal shooting is ongoing, with the three teenage suspects still being sought.Javits was chased before he was fatally shotSurveillance footage reportedly captured Javits running, as a person wearing all black trailed behind. Another angle of video footage appeared to show masked individuals in dark clothing fleeing the site of the shooting.Javits marked one year in New York after arriving from Ghana.Ghana’s minister of foreign affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, condemned the attack in a Friday statement. “We will pursue justice and we will make sure that those who did this do not get away with it.”“Just one year ago, Javits arrived in the United States from Ghana to reunite with his father and begin a new chapter of his life. Like so many Ghanaian immigrant families, his family came together in America with hopes of greater opportunity, security, and a promising future,” the Ghana diaspora public affairs collective, a US-based non-profit, also said in a Friday statement.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A Canadian family foundation has promised C$10 million (£5.5 million) to support hospital redevelopment projects in Mississauga.
articles.body: A Canadian family foundation has promised C$10 million (£5.5 million) to support hospital redevelopment projects in Mississauga. The donation will also create a dollar-for-dollar matching challenge, encouraging local residents to contribute to the projects.cThe donation from the Myhal Family Foundation will support the Built for Us campaign, a C$1 billion fundraising effort led by the Trillium Health Partners Foundation. Under the agreement, every donation made by members of the public will be matched dollar for dollar over the coming months. The money will help expand healthcare facilities across the region. According to an official announcement released by Trillium Health Partners Foundation on 29 October 2026, the funding will support several major construction and redevelopment projects across its hospital network. These include the new Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital, the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, and the expansion and redevelopment of The Gilgan Family Queensway Health Centre.A personal tribute to family legacyFor the family making the donation, the multi-million-dollar gift has a deeply personal meaning. It is linked to the care their family received from the hospital network. Rayla Myhal, President and Director of the Myhal Family Foundation, and her husband, George Myhal, made the donation in memory of Rayla's late father, Mehraj Din. Din was a respected member of the local community. He received treatment at Trillium Health Partners hospitals and strongly supported charitable giving throughout his life. Family members said Din regularly encouraged people around him to give generously and help others. The foundation hopes to continue this belief by encouraging new donors to take part in the matching campaign. “I have seen what great care can mean to a family in its hardest moments,” Rayla Myhal said in statements published by the foundation. “George and I believe that when a community comes together, it can build something none of us could build alone. We hope this gift inspires others to join us, and that every person who gives knows their contribution matters.”Driving the largest hospital expansion in CanadaThe matching campaign comes as Trillium Health Partners begins what healthcare officials describe as the largest hospital redevelopment project in Canadian history. Trillium Health Partners is Canada's largest community-based hospital network. It serves growing and diverse communities across Mississauga, West Toronto, and nearby municipalities. The hospital network has three main locations: Credit Valley Hospital, Mississauga Hospital, and the Queensway Health Centre. The expansion plans aim to replace older buildings with modern hospitals that can treat more patients and meet the expected population growth over the coming decades. The planned Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital will replace the existing Mississauga Hospital building. The new facility will have significantly more beds for patients needing hospital treatment and expanded emergency services. At the same time, the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children will provide special care facilities for children and mothers. It will include dedicated spaces for both inpatient and outpatient treatment. The redevelopment of the Queensway Health Centre will focus on expanding long-term complex care and rehabilitation services. This is expected to reduce pressure on emergency and other hospital wards across the wider network.Matching challenge to mobilize new donorsBy making the C$10 million donation a matching challenge starting on 29 October 2026, the Myhal Family Foundation hopes to encourage more people and groups to support the campaign. The fundraising effort is seeking donations from former patients who are grateful for their care, hospital employees, doctors, local businesses, and community volunteers. Healthcare leaders have stressed that donations from local communities play an important role in completing large public hospital projects. “Rayla and George have given our community something more than a gift. They've given us a catalyst that will further inspire support,” said Caroline Riseboro, President and Chief Executive Officer of Trillium Health Partners Foundation, in the press announcement. “Their gift means every donation, at every level, now goes even further in building hospitals that are truly built for us. We're deeply grateful for their leadership, and I know this community will rise to meet it.”Hospital leaders also explained that public funding often depends on additional contributions from local communities. These donations help pay for specialised medical equipment and advanced features in hospital buildings. “We have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to reimagine health care for our community and our country, creating a system that is more proactive, connected and personalized, and designed around the people it serves,” said Karli Farrow, President and Chief Executive Officer of Trillium Health Partners. “Communities build hospitals, and transformational generosity from families like the Myhals is helping us build a better, stronger future for health care. On behalf of Team THP, thank you to Rayla and George for helping bring that future to life.” The matching campaign will remain open to public donations through the hospital foundation's online donation portal and community fundraising events.You use AI every day. articles.title: Anonymous donor pledges $225 million to a US college as it launches a $450 million fundraising campaign; students could get more scholarships and financial aid
articles.summary: An anonymous donor has pledged $225 million to Centre College in Kentucky, US, to establish a fund aimed at expanding scholarship opportunities and
articles.body: An anonymous donor has pledged $225 million to Centre College in Kentucky, US, to establish a fund aimed at expanding scholarship opportunities and supporting academic excellence. Announced on October 16, 2026, the gift will anchor the institution's $450 million fundraising campaign, its most ambitious in its 207-year history. The Centre Forever Fund, created through the contribution, will provide endowed merit-based and need-based scholarships, helping talented students access higher education. The college said the donation would strengthen its mission of making a liberal arts education accessible to deserving students. The commitment comes as Centre College seeks to double its endowment and expand academic opportunities, student support and educational resources for future generations.How students could benefit from the $225 million giftThe donation will establish the Centre Forever Fund, which is designed to provide financial assistance through merit-based and need-based scholarships. Merit-based awards recognise students for academic achievement or other accomplishments, while need-based scholarships help students whose financial circumstances make college education difficult to afford.The fund is intended to make a Centre College education accessible to more deserving students by reducing financial barriers. Endowed scholarships are generally supported by investment returns generated from a fund, allowing financial assistance to continue over time.The college has not announced the number of students expected to receive scholarships or the amount individual students could receive. However, the fund is intended to strengthen access to education and support students throughout their academic journeys.College launches a $450 million fundraising campaignThe donation was announced alongside the public launch of Pillars of Excellence: The Campaign for Centre College, a $450 million fundraising initiative. The institution said it had raised $350 million from alumni, parents and supporters since the campaign's quiet phase began in 2020.The campaign aims to double the college's endowment, which was valued at approximately $450 million in the announcement. The broader initiative will support scholarships, academic programmes, technological innovation, student facilities and athletics.The $225 million commitment represents half of the campaign's overall fundraising target. The college hopes the initiative will expand educational opportunities and strengthen its long-term financial resources.Six priorities of the fundraising campaignThe campaign focuses on six areas intended to strengthen the college's academic offerings and student experience.Access and opportunity: Expanding merit-based and need-based scholarships, the Centre Promise financial aid programme, and stipends for internships and study-abroad opportunities.Academic excellence: Supporting endowed professorships, innovation laboratories and new learning spaces.Innovation and technology: Preparing students to adapt to technological developments and changing workplace demands.Career, civic and cultural leadership: Supporting programmes that encourage civil discourse, cultural engagement and leadership.Student experience and community life: Improving student accommodation, wellness resources and communal spaces.Athletics and competitive excellence: Strengthening athletic facilities and supporting student-athletes.These priorities form part of the wider $450 million campaign. The college has specifically linked the anonymous donor's gift to the Centre Forever Fund, scholarships and academic excellence.Why the donation matters for higher educationThe contribution comes at a time when the affordability of higher education remains a significant consideration for students and families. Tuition, accommodation, books and other expenses can make attending college financially challenging, particularly for students who do not have sufficient family resources.By establishing an endowed fund for scholarships, Centre College aims to strengthen its capacity to provide financial assistance over the long term. The gift could also help the institution attract talented students who might otherwise find the cost of attending a private college difficult to manage.The college has highlighted the importance of critical thinking, adaptability and communication skills associated with a liberal arts education. Its fundraising campaign aims to build on these strengths while expanding access to academic and extracurricular opportunities.What the donor said about the contributionThe donor, whose identity has not been publicly disclosed, said he and his wife believed in Centre College's mission of providing an exceptional liberal arts education to deserving students.In the college's announcement, the donor expressed hope that the contribution would encourage others to support the institution and help make a Centre education possible for every student who earns the opportunity.Centre College president Milton C. Moreland said the gift would support the institution's mission of preparing students to become leaders in their communities and beyond. Jess Metzmeier, the college's vice president for engagement and advancement, said the contribution would help expand access, affordability, educational innovation and student success.About Centre CollegeFounded in 1819, Centre College is a private liberal arts college in Danville, Kentucky. The institution offers an undergraduate education focused on academic study, faculty engagement and experiential learning.The college reports that 98% of its graduates are employed or enrolled in graduate school within a year of graduation. It has attributed its graduate outcomes to small classes, close student-faculty relationships and hands-on learning opportunities.The new fundraising campaign is intended to build on these outcomes by expanding scholarships, strengthening academic programmes and improving the student experience.The $225 million commitment marks a major development in the college's fundraising efforts, with the Centre Forever Fund expected to play a central role in supporting scholarships and academic excellence for future generations.You use AI every day. Two other girls were in the enclosure at the time, but the animal caretaker who was present took actions to protect them. articles.title: Kid Rock reveals what he told French President Macron after Trump unexpectedly handed him phone on golf course
articles.summary: Kid Rock told Bill Maher how a golf outing with Trump ended with him holding the phone mid-call with Emmanuel Macron in a viral "Real Time" moment.
articles.body: Musician Kid Rock drew laughs from comedian Bill Maher's audience as he recounted how a golf outing with President Donald Trump ended with the singer on the phone with French President Emmanuel Macron. During Friday's episode of HBO's "Real Time with Bill Maher," Kid Rock said he was golfing with Trump when the president handed him a phone with Macron on the line. "That was funny. Yeah, we’re out golfing. I hate speaking out of school, but this is just a fun one," Kid Rock said. He told Maher that Trump was taking calls throughout their golf outing. DAVID MARCUS: BILL MAHER'S NO REPUBLICAN, HE'S JUST A RARE DEMOCRAT WHO THINKS "The guy’s taking calls all day," Kid Rock said. "He’s working while you’re golfing. This guy does not stop working. We can all agree on that. He sleeps maybe four or five hours a night. So we’re out there, Macron calls, we’re out there, [Trump’s] talking to him." Kid Rock -- whose real name is Robert Ritchie -- then described how Trump handed him the phone while he stood beside the president's golf cart. "We’re all standing there," Kid Rock continued. [Trump’s] like, ‘Hey, I’m here with the great Kid Rock,’ like Macron knows who I am, and he’s like, ‘Bob, say hello.’" "So he gives me the phone and I’m like, ‘Hello, Mr. President,’" he added. "And I’m like, ‘I’m from the Paris of the Midwest: Detroit.’ And Trump leaves, he gets in the golf cart." BILL MAHER FIRES BACK AT LIBERAL CRITICS OVER SECOND TRUMP DINNER Maher laughed as Kid Rock described the exchange, telling the audience, "He leaves Macron on the phone with Kid Rock." Kid Rock concluded the story by mimicking his conversation with Macron, adding, "I was like, ‘So what else you been up to?'" Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment. The musician’s recounting of the phone call drew laughs from Maher, Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) and journalist Jim VandeHei. The anecdote came during an episode in which Maher also fired back at a lengthy Truth Social post from Trump criticizing the comedian following their second White House dinner. Kid Rock and ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith also attended the dinner. "It’s a lot of fun at the time but later on, they’re tearing you a new a------." Kid Rock’s story — and Maher’s apparent prompting — drew the ire of Democratic political strategist Kaivon Shroff, who told Fox News Digital the comedian’s knee-slapping was anything but candid. "If Barack Obama had handed Emmanuel Macron off to some celebrity on a golf course and driven away, Maher would have gone on a ten-minute rant about how unserious, embarrassing and beneath the presidency it was," Shroff said. "Trump does it and suddenly Maher is pounding the table laughing like it is the funniest thing he has ever heard." articles.title: District of Columbia and Virginia sue to block Trump’s triumphal arch plans
articles.summary: The monument has sparked fierce opposition from local governments fearing disruption to traffic and historic views.
articles.body:
The District of Columbia (DC) and the state of Virginia have filed a joint lawsuit to halt the construction of a large triumphal arch sought by United States President Donald Trump.

Filed on Saturday, the lawsuit denounces the project as “flagrantly unlawful” and “legally indefensible”.

It calls on the federal court system to bar construction before it starts.

Otherwise, the lawsuit warns, Trump could claim that pausing construction already under way would pose a national security risk, as he has done with other controversial projects in the past.

“This is not the first time that Defendants have rushed to dramatically remake the District too quickly for courts to intervene,” the lawsuit reads. “This Court should not allow this effort to escape judicial scrutiny.”

Saturday’s complaint brings the total number of lawsuits against the arch to three.

Trump has championed the prospect of building a triumphal arch, similar to the Arc de Triomphe built in Paris during Napoleonic times.

Trump’s arch, however, is designed to stand 30 metres (100 feet) taller than the Statue of Liberty. It would tower from the Memorial Circle in Washington, DC, at 76 metres (250ft).

That colossal scale has prompted outrage, particularly from veterans’ groups who fear the arch would block views of Arlington National Cemetery, a hallowed military grave site.

White House officials maintain that ground could be broken as early as next week, on or around November 5.

On Friday, the administration unveiled a 106-page proposal for the arch to be a 12-storey megastructure, featuring a winged bronze statue of Lady Liberty lifting an eternal flame.

The arch would include two mezzanines and an observation deck with panoramic east-west views, as well as programme spaces, offices and a “fire command centre”.

Trump has previously said the arch would double as a military hub with snipers and drone capabilities.

Construction on the arch would also result in significant traffic changes in the area, including rerouting traffic to nearby roads.

In Saturday’s lawsuit, Attorneys General Brian Schwalb of Washington, DC, and Jay Jones of Virginia pointed to the project’s disruptive footprint as a major concern.

“As soon as defendants break ground on this project, they will inflict irreparable harm on both the District and Virginia,” the lawsuit said.

It warns that the anticipated three-year construction project will stymie commuter traffic, slow down emergency vehicles and generate significant pollution, including “stormwater runoff into the Potomac”.

The lawsuit calls on the court to force the Trump administration to get congressional authorisation before any construction can begin.

The new legal challenge comes on the heels of an October 8 filing by Arlington County, which was the first governmental body to mount a legal action against Trump’s planned monument.

In that lawsuit, the county’s governing board argued that the project would cause “significant harm” to its residents and likely require changes to nearby flight paths.

The first complaint came in February, when a group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian launched an effort to stop the arch.

District Judge Tanya Chutkan is overseeing that case, and she is weighing whether to issue a preliminary injunction to temporarily freeze any construction plans while the court hears arguments.

At a hearing on Friday, Chutkan deferred an immediate ruling but signalled that she would be issuing a decision expeditiously.

She previously ordered the administration to give the court 48 hours’ notice before undertaking any activities related to the construction of the arch.

The monument has already received early approval from the US Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were all tapped by Trump.

articles.title: In Gurgaon, rain gives second straight clean air day, but relief may not last
articles.summary: Gurgaon AQI stayed satisfactory at 88 after heavy October rain (67.9mm), but SAFAR warns drier weather and cooling may push air to moderate Sunday, poor Monday.
articles.body: Gurgaon: The city continued to enjoy relatively clean air for the second consecutive day on Saturday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) remaining in the “satisfactory” category, largely due to rainfall that has made October unusually wet. However, the respite is likely to be short-lived, with drier weather and falling temperatures expected to push the AQI into the moderate category on Sunday and poor from Monday.The city’s AQI was recorded at 88 on Saturday, up from 69 on Friday. All four monitoring stations reported satisfactory readings, with Gwal Pahari and Vikas Sadan recording an AQI of 71 each, followed by Sector 51 at 93 and Teri Gram at 97.This was the third day this month when the city’s AQI remained in the satisfactory category. In October last year, Gurgaon recorded five such days, with the lowest AQI at 58. In 2024, there were four satisfactory days, with the lowest reading at 59, while October 2023 saw only one such day, when the AQI stood at 97.Despite the favourable overall AQI, particulate matter concentrations at individual monitoring stations remained considerably high. Gwal Pahari recorded a PM2.5 concentration of 119 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³), nearly eight times the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended safe limit of 15 µg/m³. Teri Gram recorded 278 µg/m³, Sector 51 247 µg/m³ and Vikas Sadan 61 µg/m³.PM10 levels were also elevated across all four stations. Sector 51 recorded the highest concentration at 387 µg/m³, followed by Teri Gram at 185 µg/m³, Vikas Sadan at 130 µg/m³ and Gwal Pahari at 124 µg/m³. All readings exceeded the WHO’s recommended threshold of 45 µg/m³. The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) prescribes annual limits of 60 µg/m³ for PM2.5 and 100 µg/m³ for PM10.According to the System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research (SAFAR), surface winds on Sunday are likely to blow predominantly from the northwest, reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph.“The maximum mixing depth is likely to be 1,500 metres, and the ventilation index is likely to be 9,000 m²/s on Sunday. A ventilation index below 6,000 m²/s, with an average wind speed under 10 kmph, is considered unfavourable for the dispersion of pollutants,” it stated.SAFAR forecast moderate air quality for Sunday, with the AQI likely to deteriorate to the poor category from Monday.The rainfall has made this one of the wettest Octobers Gurgaon has recorded in recent years. The city received 67.9 mm of rainfall this month, 680% above its normal October precipitation of 8.7 mm. This is the second-highest October rainfall in a decade, after 80.9 mm recorded in 2022.This year’s rainfall is more than double the 30.9 mm recorded in October 2025 and over 10 times the 6.7 mm received in 2023. The city recorded 28.8 mm in 2021, while October 2024 remained completely dry.Across Haryana, the average rainfall stood at 34.6 mm in October, 268% above the normal 9.4 mm. This was the third-highest October rainfall in the state in 25 years, after 52.5 mm in 2004 and 35.9 mm in 2022.Meanwhile, maximum temperatures rose sharply on Saturday as skies cleared and sunshine returned. NorthCap University recorded a maximum of 29°C, up 8.5 degrees from the previous day. Gurgaon AWS recorded 26.9°C, an increase of 6.9 degrees, while Gurgaon KVK logged 27.2°C.Minimum temperatures at Gurgaon AWS and NorthCap University stood at 14.9°C and 17.1°C, compared with 17.2°C and 17.8°C, respectively, on Friday. Gurgaon KVK recorded a minimum of 19.1°C, up from 17.9°C.NorthCap University received 3 mm of rainfall, while Gurgaon AWS recorded 2 mm till 8.30 am on Saturday.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: School murder trial stays in Gurgaon, HC rejects CBI bid to move it to Panchkula
articles.summary: Punjab and Haryana HC keeps 2017 Gurgaon school murder trial in Gurgaon, rejects CBI move to Panchkula, says CBI court lacks jurisdiction.
articles.body: Gurgaon: The Punjab and Haryana high court has ordered the 2017 Gurgaon school murder trial to remain in the city, rejecting CBI’s plea to shift it to its special court in Panchkula. It ruled that the investigating agency’s administrative convenience cannot override the Juvenile Justice Act’s safeguards or give its special court jurisdiction to try a murder case.Justice Manisha Batra observed that the accused student must be tried by a children’s court under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act. The court also rejected the alternative request to shift the proceedings to a children’s court in Panchkula, saying no grounds had been established to justify moving the trial out of Gurgaon.It directed the additional sessions judge heading the Gurgaon children’s court to “make every endeavour to conclude the trial”, preferably within six months of receiving a certified copy of the order, subject to cooperation from the parties.On Sept 8, 2017, a Class 2 student – referred to in court records by the fictitious name ‘Prince’ – was found murdered in a ground-floor washroom of an English-medium school in the city. Police initially arrested the school’s bus conductor, Ashok Kumar. But after taking over the probe, CBI said it found no evidence against him and sought his discharge. The trial court allowed the plea in Feb 2018.CBI had, meanwhile, apprehended another student from the same school, identified as ‘Bholu’ in court records. He was in Class XI and below 18 at the time of the murder. After CBI alleged that he killed the younger boy, Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) conducted a preliminary assessment and ordered that he be tried as an adult. The decision, however, went through successive legal challenges, including before the Supreme Court.After the high court ordered a fresh assessment, JJB again directed an adult trial in Oct 2022. The high court upheld that decision in May 2023, paving the way for the case to proceed before the children’s court in the city.CBI later sought to transfer the trial to its special judge in Panchkula, arguing that the court exercised jurisdiction over CBI cases across Haryana. It also pointed out that proceedings against adult accused arising from the same FIR were pending there. Moving records and prosecution witnesses to Gurgaon, it said, was causing inconvenience. The boy’s father supported the plea, arguing that evidence in the connected cases should be considered together. Haryana govt also raised no objection.But Sushil Tekriwal, counsel for the victim’s family, opposed the transfer, arguing that sections 1(4) and 18(3) of the JJ Act made a children’s court the mandatory forum. CBI’s notifications, he submitted, authorised the agency to investigate but did not confer trial jurisdiction on its special court. He also pointed out that proceedings in Gurgaon had progressed substantially and a transfer could cause further delay.The high court accepted the objection about central jurisdiction. It said Haryana govt’s Feb 8, 2012, notification appointing the presiding officer of the Panchkula CBI court as a special judge was issued under the Prevention of Corruption Act and covered offences under that law. The murder charge under Section 302 of IPC did not fall within its scope.The court clarified that Haryana and central govt notifications issued in Sept 2017, which enabled CBI to take over the probe, dealt with investigative powers alone. They did not change the court before which the case had to be tried. Under the ordinary rule, a crime is tried by a court within whose jurisdiction it was committed.Justice Batra also referred to Section 19 of the JJ Act, which requires a children’s court to consider the child’s special needs, ensure a child-friendly atmosphere and fair trial, and provide for an individual care plan and safeguards related to rehabilitation. These obligations, the court said, could not be discharged by a CBI special court merely because its presiding officer held the rank of a sessions judge.It further relied on Section 23, which bars joint proceedings against a child in conflict with law and an adult accused. “The trials arising from the same FIR must therefore remain separate. Common witnesses can be examined independently in each,” the court observed.Rejecting the argument about the inconvenience of transporting records and witnesses, the court said transfer pleas must account for the convenience of all parties — the accused, complainant, prosecution and witnesses — not just the investigating agency. The victim’s family, accused and school were based in Gurgaon, where the trial had already proceeded for years. There was also no material to suggest that a fair and impartial hearing was impossible there, it held.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Washington's Ruby City once had more than 1,000 residents during a silver rush; today the historic townsite lies among the state's forested hills
articles.summary: Once a thriving silver-mining settlement with more than 1,000 residents, Ruby City was at the centre of Washington’s mining boom in the late 19th century.
articles.body: Once a thriving silver-mining settlement with more than 1,000 residents, Ruby City was at the centre of Washington’s mining boom in the late 19th century. Prospectors, investors and businesses flocked to the town as silver discoveries fuelled hopes of prosperity. However, declining silver prices, limited mineral deposits and high transport costs eventually brought its mining industry to a halt. Today, the former settlement is known as Old Ruby State Park Heritage Site, where forested hills and tall ponderosa pines surround a townsite with no standing buildings remaining. According to the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission, the site preserves the history of a once-busy community whose fortunes rose and fell with the silver rush.How Washington’s Ruby City grew during the silver rush in 1886 and 1887The opening of the former reservation lands for mineral claims and settlement on 1 May 1886 encouraged further prospecting. Four months later, Fred Wendt discovered the Nevada vein north of the future townsite and persuaded investors to join him in developing the prospect through the War Eagle Mining and Milling Company. John Cluman and James Milliken subsequently staked the Last Chance claim, while three miners discovered the First Thought claim in October 1886. According to Washington State Parks, the First Thought mine eventually developed more than 4,000 feet of underground passages across three levels and produced silver ore valued at more than $2.5 million in 2025 terms.As mining activity expanded, William Singleton and Thomas D. Fuller established Ruby City on land along Salmon Creek on 6 January 1887. The town was laid out with Main Street running parallel to the creek, while Ruby Street and Salmon Street lay to the west and east, respectively. Numbered streets extended from First Street at the northern end to Tenth Street at the southern end. Lots were offered for sale, and businesses developed to serve miners and other residents. However, the commission records that Singleton and Fuller did not initially own the land they were selling, leading residents to demand that the developers obtain legal title. The ownership dispute was not fully resolved until 17 March 1892.Ruby City’s businesses and banking industry fueled its silver rush boomRuby City’s growth extended beyond its mines. Businesses supplied goods and services to the mining population, while the town developed financial and social establishments. Sam Lichtenstadter opened the Bank of Ruby, which issued distinctive pink checks because it had limited supplies of US cash. According to the state parks account, nearly $300,000 worth of these checks were once in circulation across central Washington and British Columbia. The town also had a brewery and several saloons, including the Mother Lode Saloon, the Office Saloon, the Silver Corner, the Snug Saloon and the Bachelors Saloon.Ruby City briefly became the seat of the newly established Okanogan County in 1888. The Washington Territorial Legislature approved the creation of the county on 2 February that year, and the county commissioners met to organise its government in March. Ruby City was selected as the county seat, but voters later chose to transfer that position to Conconully. The town’s promoters continued to advertise its commercial importance. In 1890, the Ruby Land Company described it as the “business center of the greatest mining region in the State of Washington”, highlighting its business activity and a reported monthly payroll of $10,000. Despite these claims, Ruby remained remote, and attempts to secure railway service or better roads were unsuccessful.Why Washington’s Ruby City declined after the silver rushThe limitations of the mineral deposits became increasingly apparent within a decade of Ruby City’s founding. According to Washington State Parks, the silver-bearing veins extended only limited distances, restricting the amount of ore that could be extracted. Transport expenses also reduced the profitability of mining. Ore was typically hauled by wagon for 45 miles to Brewster, transferred to riverboats for an 80-mile journey to Wenatchee, and then moved onto railway cars bound for smelters in Tacoma or Montana.The commission also identifies wider economic developments as a factor in the town’s collapse. The Sherman Silver Purchase Act, enacted by the US Congress on 14 July 1890, increased the federal government’s required silver purchases and gave mining activity a temporary boost. However, the agency explains that the resulting increase in circulating dollars, without corresponding growth in government gold stocks, eventually contributed to a fall in silver prices. Together with global economic trends, this helped bring about the Panic of 1893. Mining operations in Ruby City subsequently failed. Ellensburg mayor Austin Mires visited in August 1899 and recorded that “the town was entirely deserted”. By 1904, only a few deteriorating buildings remained.Ruby City’s silver mines reopened but struggled with transport costsMining did not end permanently with the first collapse. Operations resumed at the Arlington, First Thought and Last Chance mines in the early 1920s, and several shipments of ore were completed. However, the cost of transporting the material continued to make mining unprofitable, and the operations closed again. A concentrating mill was constructed at the Arlington Mine in 1936 to process ore on site and reduce shipping costs. Mining continued until 1940, when operations stopped.Efforts to preserve Ruby City’s history began decades later. Washington State Parks records that the Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission started systematically identifying and preserving historic sites and buildings in the late 1950s. Following the allocation of preservation funding under Referendum 28, the commission began prioritising the acquisition of the former townsite. In May and June 1977, it purchased portions of nine blocks from four sellers for $44,300. Today, the site is known as Old Ruby State Park Heritage Site. The commission states that “No standing structures remain”, and the only development at the park site is an interpretive sign maintained by the Okanogan County Historical Society. The former mining settlement is therefore documented through its historical record and the preserved townsite rather than surviving buildings.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Widowed and divorced daughters returning to live with parents can now be added to their parents' Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) cards, even after the death of the govt employee or pensioner in whose name the original card was issued. Health ministry has allowed eligible daughters to be added or reinstated in cards held by family pensioners.The move will help parents supporting daughters with no independent income who need medical care. Earlier, once the original cardholder died and the spouse began receiving family pension, there was no provision to add or reinstate dependent family members.The ministry said it had received representations from pensioners facing difficulties supporting such daughters, particularly those with serious medical conditions requiring continued treatment. The benefit will not be automatic: authorities will verify daughter's marital status, income and dependency.All other CGHS eligibility conditions will continue to apply, the Oct 28 order said. articles.title: Cruise company founder says he's 'the villain' after 200-plus passengers are stranded
articles.summary: The cruise ship captain of the Villa Vie Odyssey calls the forced disembarkation in Cambodia "really painful" as over 200 residents now face an uncertain future.
articles.body: The captain of the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship is speaking out after 203 residents were forced to disembark in Cambodia due to a critical fuel shortage, calling the ordeal "really painful." The ship, which offered passengers the chance to make the ocean their permanent home, suspended its around-the-world voyage earlier this week after soaring fuel costs made continued operations financially unsustainable, according to its operator. Residents were forced to leave the vessel in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, just two years after the ship set sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland, on what was supposed to be a 3 1/2-year journey around the world. THOUSANDS BOOKED TROPICAL BAHAMAS CRUISE AND ENDED UP IN FREEZING CANADA INSTEAD "I feel awful. They’re counting on me to make the decisions here, and there’s nothing else I’m focused on. I’m the villain in the story, but I’m doing everything I can to support the residents [with] a solution," Mikael Petterson, founder and executive chairman of Villa Vie Residences, told Business Insider. Some residents had paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the chance to live aboard. Villa Vie Residences had offered lifetime access to the ship through its "Endless Horizons" program for a one-time payment of $299,999 for a single-occupancy cabin or $499,999 for double occupancy, Fox Business reported in May 2024. Captain Emanuele Giudice on Thursday opened up about what led to the decision to force residents off the ship. "Unfortunately, due to the shortage of fuel, we needed to shut down one generator, chiller, non-essential lights," Giudice said, as Reuters reported. CRUISE PASSENGERS FACE BLOCKED ACCESS AS ANGRY PROTESTERS SET BARRICADES ON FIRE Giudice said the shutdowns would have "created discomfort to the residents, which — we don't want that." "So we kindly asked the residents to get off the ship because our fuel situation was critical," he said. "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do." Asked who was to blame, Giudice pointed to high fuel prices, saying they had significantly affected the ship's travel. CRUISE FEE DOUBLES AT VACATION HOT SPOT AS PASSENGERS BRACE FOR EVEN STEEPER HIKES He declined to comment when a reporter asked whether the war in the Middle East and President Donald Trump were responsible. Giudice also said residents were given more than 24 hours' notice to leave the ship. Yet passengers previously told The Associated Press (AP) they received just seven hours' notice and had to make their own accommodations. Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming, previously told AP they were repeatedly asked for fuel money. "I’m the villain in the story, but I’m doing everything I can to support the residents on a solution." "We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything," Lynn Montoya said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "We had hopes, but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole," she added. Benjamin Schatz, a retiree who had hoped to make the MV Odyssey his forever home, told CBS News he was devastated after being forced to leave the ship. "Honestly, right now, I'm in denial and in shock, and I'm heartbroken," Schatz said, as CBS reported. He added, "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The company had marketed life aboard the Odyssey as an alternative to traditional retirement, appealing to retirees concerned about inflation, rising living expenses and the possibility of outliving their savings. Petterson promoted the experience as a way for retirees to live on a fixed budget without worrying about ongoing expenses. articles.title: On Day of the Dead, tourists bump shoulders with celebrating families in San Andrés Mixquic
articles.summary: As night falls over the cemetery in San Andrés Mixquic, a historic village on the outskirts of Mexico City, the family of Ángel Jiménez del Águila huddles around his grave.
articles.body: As night falls over the cemetery in San Andrés Mixquic, a historic village on the outskirts of Mexico City, the family of Ángel Jiménez del Águila huddles around his grave. “Salucita for our dead,” says Jesús, one of Ángel’s sons, raising a toast to his father, who died in 2010. Only a few hours remain before the door between the world of the living and the dead opens: the family has gathered to honor Ángel during the Day of the Dead, a traditional Mexican celebration of departed loved ones held November 1 and 2. After days of cleaning graves and decorating headstones with marigolds, the cemetery here in San Andrés Mixquic is filled with the scent of copal incense and burning candles. It’s also filled with tourists: dozens from around the world wander through the cemetery, camera flashes popping as they attempt close-up shots of families celebrating in the dusk. The village’s efforts to preserve one of Mexico’s most iconic celebrations often draw these tourists searching for authentic experiences. But the influx also risks turning mourning into a spectacle, locals say, as visitors outnumber locals. Martha Nashieli, one of Ángel’s daughters, remembers arriving at the cemetery to lay flowers at father’s grave a few years ago, only to be forced to wait outside due to the volume of visitors. “They wouldn’t let me in,” Martha says. “I was frustrated because he’s my dad, I’m from here, and they weren’t letting me enter because there were seas of people.” A cemetery at capacity The Day of the Dead’s central celebration occurs in Mexican cemeteries and graveyards, where families gather around the tombstones to honor their departed loved ones with songs, incense and votive offerings. It is often erroneously compared to Halloween, though the two holidays may share ancestry in Catholicism’s All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day. Others believe the Day of the Dead is uniquely Mexican, with some experts postulating that its origins go back thousands of years. Martha, 40, grew up seeing tourists among the headstones. Since childhood, she’s accompanied her family every November 2 to visit her grandparents’ graves, surrounded by outsiders. “Suddenly, something intimate becomes — I wouldn’t want to put it this way — but it becomes a spectacle, doesn’t it?” Martha says. “And this is something intimate, something very private. At each grave, there’s a sense of communion.” Martha knows visitors are part of Mixquic’s story, and she doesn’t want them to stop coming. As she sees it, the dilemma is how to share a tradition they want the world to know about – without losing the space and intimacy that keeps it alive. “The truth is, there just isn’t enough room for all of us anymore,” she says. “We’re very cramped. Our cemetery…well, there’s simply no room for more people.” In 2025, around 100,000 people visited the cemetery between October 31 and November 2, according to Mexico City government figures — roughly seven times the village’s population, all in three days. ‘Like little animals in a zoo’ In the past, authorities installed a bridge over the cemetery so visitors could look down at the graves without occupying the space where families carry out their rituals, recalls Driselda Sánchez-Aguirre, a professor at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), who has studied mass tourism in Mixquic. The measure drew criticism because some residents felt they were being watched “like little animals in a zoo,” she says, and the bridge was ultimately used only once. Today, the only measures in place are recommendations in Mexico City’s official tourism guide, which advises visitors to ask families for permission before taking photographs and to avoid using flash. Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada has also acknowledged that the Mixquic cemetery lacks sufficient space for burials and pledged to work toward a solution – but the initiative does not explicitly address tourism. Simply asking tourists to respect the cemetery is not enough, according to Sánchez-Aguirre. “When the cemetery exceeds its physical capacity, individual responsibility gets lost in the crowd,” she explains. When visitors see others using flash photography, speaking loudly, or stepping on graves to get a better angle, they may start to think that “this is what everyone does.” As an alternative, she proposes preparing visitors before they enter the cemetery by giving them clear instructions on how to behave: “You are entering a sacred space where families keep vigil over their loved ones,” she says, describing the message visitors should receive. “This is not a spectacle.” Martha maintains that visitors from around the world have a role to play in these special days – so long as they are respectful. In her view, their curiosity about the Day of the Dead helps keep the tradition alive. “It becomes a kind of communion,” she told CNN during last year’s celebrations. “Even if we don’t know them, we know they come with respect and a desire to learn about our traditions. So, we invite them to come respectfully – to come live our tradition, to get to know it, to preserve it, to take it back to their own homes.”

articles.title: Heavy rains expected to bring flooding risk to already saturated parts of the U.S. Southwest
articles.summary: Heavy rains starting Saturday evening were expected to bring a threat of flash flooding to already saturated areas of the U.S.
articles.body: Heavy rains starting Saturday evening were expected to bring a threat of flash flooding to already saturated areas of the U.S. Southwest through Monday, according to the National Weather Service. As much as 4 inches (10 centimeters) of rain could fall across the region, where a number of weather systems have brought a deadly autumn of soaking rains. In the Phoenix area on Friday evening, emergency crews rescued people from several vehicles on flooded streets. “It’s not going to take much rainfall to be impactful at all in some of these locations just because of how saturated they are,” said Allison Santorelli, a meteorologist with the Weather Prediction Center in College Park, Maryland. The National Weather Service has issued flood watches for nearly all of Arizona and parts of southern Utah, southwestern Colorado, and western New Mexico, in addition to part of southern Nevada. Those watches include the Four Corners region, a sparsely populated area where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet that has been hit especially hard by recent rains. Santorelli said this weekend’s rain was expected to bring both flash flooding and small-stream river flooding. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, with opposition parties expecting a turnout of up to 10 lakh people and police deploying more than 4,000 personnel to manage security and crowds.The rally is being organised to protest against alleged electoral irregularities and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The mobilisation comes amid the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chori' and large-scale voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.'Chalo Dilli' march to precede rallyThe programme will begin with a march, called 'Chalo Dilli', from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan at noon. articles.title: At nine, Ethan Sanborn was building Kiid Coffee with his father; by 2026, the young founder’s beverage brand had reached more than 400 retailers
articles.summary: While most kids his age were still figuring out what they liked, Ethan Sanborn was helping his father build a beverage business.
articles.body: While most kids his age were still figuring out what they liked, Ethan Sanborn was helping his father build a beverage business. What started as a family endeavour to create a coffee-flavored drink for kids has gradually blossomed into Kiid Coffee, a growing brand that got national exposure from the TV show Shark Tank. By 2026, the company had expanded its retail presence to more than 400 stores, giving the young founder an opportunity to take a childhood idea into the wider consumer market.Ethan Sanborn established Kiid Coffee with his fatherThe Sanborn family had a personal insight that led to the creation of Kiid Coffee. Ethan liked the taste of his father's coffee and sometimes wanted some himself. But a little boy would not do for traditional coffee. So David Sanborn, his father, began to investigate a different sort of beverage.Ethan also broke both his legs separately, according to Food Republic. Later the family learned that nutritional deficiencies were a contributor and began paying more attention to his diet. So David started working on a drink that would have the similar coffee-inspired flavour that Ethan liked, but also other nutrients.The project eventually developed into a business. All Shark Tank Products reports that the company was founded in July 2023 and officially launched in April 2024. Ethan, who was 7 when the concept was developed, played an important part in shaping the product.Rather than creating another sugary drink aimed at children, the father-son team wanted to introduce something that could become part of a morning routine. The result was a powdered beverage that combined decaffeinated coffee with cacao, prebiotic fibre, vitamins and minerals.What made the drink different from conventional children's beveragesKiid Coffee was designed to offer more than the flavour of a regular coffee drink. Its original formulation included organic decaffeinated Arabica coffee, raw cacao, prebiotic fibre and a blend of vitamins and minerals. These included calcium, magnesium, iron, zinc and vitamins A, C, D3, E, B6 and B12.The product was also developed with children's dietary preferences in mind. It contained no added sugar and was designed to be dairy-free, soy-free and gluten-free. Its decaffeination process used water rather than chemicals, with the finished drink described as 99.9% caffeine-free.Parents could prepare it by mixing the powdered beverage with milk or water. The product was available in 3 initial flavours: Original Coffee, Caramel and Chocolate. The flavours were intended to make the drink appealing to children while providing nutrients that might otherwise be missing from their diets.Ethan’s younger brother Logan also helped out in the development process by tasting different batches. Their feedback helped the family refine the flavours, with the Chocolate version resembling hot cocoa and Caramel offering a sweeter taste.How did Kiid Coffee secure a deal on Shark TankThe father-son team took their idea to ABC's Shark Tank in March 2025. According to Food Republic, David and 8-year-old Ethan entered the programme seeking $50,000 in exchange for a 5% stake in their business.During the presentation, the pair explained the product and its intended benefits. The Sharks sampled the different flavours before discussing the company's sales, production costs and plans for growth.Food Republic reported that the drink was being sold for $14, while its production cost was approximately $3.50. Since its launch in 2024, the company has sold $75,000 in products, much of it through direct-to-consumer online sales and Amazon.The presentation attracted the attention of several investors. Kevin O’Leary offered $50,000 for 30%, Lori Greiner and Mark Cuban together offered $50,000 for 20%. Daniel Lubetzky, the founder of KIND Snacks, also offered $50,000 for a 20% share.Ethan attempted to negotiate a smaller equity arrangement, asking for 10% in exchange for the investment. However, after discussing the proposals with his father, he accepted Lubetzky's offer. The agreement also included an additional 5% in stock options if David moved from his part-time involvement to working full-time on the company.The deal provided the young business with an investor who had experience building a consumer food brand. It also gave Kiid Coffee greater visibility beyond its existing online customer base.The business expanded beyond its early online customersThe television appearance brought Kiid Coffee considerable attention. Food Republic reported that the company received thousands of orders shortly after the episode aired.Its retail expansion followed quickly. By August 2025, Kiid Coffee was available in more than 150 stores, according to Food Republic. A social media update from August 15, 2025, described the business as a $1 million-a-year company.The growth continued into 2026. In a press release published through PR Newswire, Kiid Coffee announced that it had expanded into more than 400 retail locations across the United States. The company had also entered grocery chains such as Raley's in the Northwest and Fresh Thyme Market in the Midwest.The same announcement stated that the business had surpassed $2 million in annualised sales within 10 months and was on track to exceed $2 million in annual revenue. These figures reflected its projected business performance rather than a confirmed annual financial result.The product range had also grown from three flavours to 5. Alongside Original, Caramel and Chocolate, customers could choose S'mores and Minty Mocha. The company also announced plans for a caffeine-free tea range, extending its focus beyond coffee-inspired drinks.Ethan and David have plans beyond the original productKiid Coffee's development has also involved teaching children about business and food choices. The family has used Ethan's involvement to show how a product can move from an idea to manufacturing, sales and distribution.David brought previous business experience to the venture. According to All Shark Tank Products, he studied polymer and fibre engineering at Georgia Tech and had established his first consumer brand in 2012. He later launched a pet food seasoning business in 2016, which he scaled and sold in 2020. That experience helped him understand product development and online sales before starting Kiid Coffee.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Three falcons died and eggs were damaged after building work near a £150,000 prize-winning falcon; a £500,000 neighbour dispute now faces a potential Supreme Court appeal
articles.summary: Three falcons died and eggs were damaged after building work near a neighbouring aviary in Cornwall, sparking a legal dispute that has left former reality
articles.body: Three falcons died and eggs were damaged after building work near a neighbouring aviary in Cornwall, sparking a legal dispute that has left former reality TV contestant Barnes Thomas facing a reported bill of around £500,000, as reported by The Independent. Thomas, who appeared on Bear Grylls’ survival programme The Island in 2018, was sued by falcon breeders Martin and Scott Nicholas, whose business operated beside his land. One of the dead birds was valued at £150,000. The Court of Appeal overturned the finding of private nuisance but upheld Thomas’s liability in negligence. The dispute has since moved towards a potential Supreme Court appeal, with both sides challenging aspects of the ruling.Why a former reality TV star’s move to Cornwall ended in a £500,000 legal battleThomas moved from dealing in art in London to farming near St Just, close to Land’s End. The change of setting did not bring a quiet life. His relationship with neighbours Martin Nicholas, 43, and Scott Nicholas, 45, deteriorated as disagreements developed over activities on his property. The brothers ran Raptors of Penwith Ltd, a falcon-breeding business on adjoining land, where they raised gyr and peregrine falcons for sale to racing enthusiasts, including buyers in Dubai.The disagreement eventually became a legal battle involving both the use of the land and the potential consequences for the birds kept next door. The brothers maintained that building work on Thomas’s property had exposed their falcons to excessive noise and visual disturbance during a particularly sensitive period. They also alleged that the activity had affected breeding, resulting in lost eggs and damage to eggs caused by distressed birds. Their company brought claims for nuisance and negligence against Thomas and Upper Cot Estate Limited, his company.The High Court in Bristol heard the case over nine days in 2025. Judge Jonathan Russen KC found in favour of the falcon breeders, concluding that the conduct of Thomas and his company had caused the deaths of three gyr falcons. As reported by The Independent, the financial consequences were substantial: approximately £300,000 in compensation and interest, alongside more than £180,000 towards the breeders’ legal expenses. Thomas was also responsible for his own legal costs.How construction work during breeding season disturbed the neighbouring falconsThe dispute was not simply about whether building work was permissible on agricultural land. The court had to consider how that work was conducted and whether reasonable precautions had been taken to avoid disturbing the neighbouring birds.According to the High Court judgment, Thomas had been told that the period from March to June was a time when excessive noise and visual disturbance should be avoided. Evidence included videos recorded inside the falcons’ incubation room while work was taking place in a barn. The judge considered that material evidence of the effect the construction activity was having on the birds.A particular incident involved a JCB digger bucket being left raised for three days close to the aviary. The machine was positioned for an engineer’s inspection, but its location meant it obstructed the line of sight from at least some of the birds in the western pens. Scott Nicholas said the falcons reacted strongly to the sight of the machinery, describing their response as becoming agitated at what appeared to them to be an unfamiliar object.The judge accepted that the activity had caused undue disturbance. He found that the three birds had died as a result of stress associated with the nuisance and concluded that the work had been undertaken without proper consideration of the breeding operation next door.The legal argument over property rights and a neighbouring falcon businessThomas challenged the ruling on the grounds that it placed an unreasonable restriction on how he could use his own property. His barrister, Tom Weekes KC, argued before the Court of Appeal in February 2026 that the construction of a barn and the storage of materials for Thomas’s scaffolding business were ordinary uses of land.The appeal raised a question about the extent to which one landowner should have to accommodate a neighbouring business that depends on particularly sensitive conditions. Weekes argued that the falcon breeders’ activities should not effectively require Thomas to maintain a buffer zone on his own property to protect their birds.The judges disagreed on the legal basis for liabilityThe Court of Appeal dismissed Thomas’s appeal on negligence but allowed it on nuisance grounds, with each issue decided 2-1. Lady Justice Whipple found that Thomas and Upper Cot Estate Limited were liable for both nuisance and negligence. Lord Justice Nugee concluded that negligence had been established, while Lord Justice Moylan would have found neither form of liability.Lord Justice Nugee accepted that parking a digger on one’s own land was an ordinary activity. However, he considered the circumstances surrounding its placement to be decisive. The machine did not have to be left next to the aviary, and even if that location had been necessary for the engineer’s visit, the bucket should not have been left raised.His reasoning focused on whether Thomas and his company had acted with appropriate care. The judge considered that reasonable alternatives were available and that leaving the machinery in that position was unnecessary for the defendants’ purposes. The failure to take reasonable steps to avoid inconvenience to the neighbouring business supported the finding of negligence.Lady Justice Whipple agreed with the conclusion on negligence, stating that Thomas and his company should not be able to disregard their neighbours’ interests in the way they had done. She also referred to the earlier findings of fact, noting that the trial judge had rejected the defendants’ evidence and expert opinion.A dispute that had already affected the wider neighbourhoodThe falcon case formed part of a broader disagreement between Thomas and people living around his property. During the High Court proceedings, Judge Russen described the conflict as bitter and said it had gained momentum over a relatively short period.Thomas had also encountered opposition over other activities on his land, including the creation of a lake and the temporary removal of a stile on a public footpath. These incidents contributed to tensions beyond the immediate dispute with the Nicholas brothers. The compensation awarded by the High Court addressed the losses established in relation to the dead falcons, while the appeal focused on whether Thomas and his company could properly be held responsible.One of the dead birds had been valued at £150,000 and had previously won races. The figure illustrated the financial stakes involved, although the court’s decision rested on its findings about liability rather than the value of that bird alone.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump loses legal battle over Epstein-linked Wall Street Journal case
articles.summary: Judge permanently drops Trump’s $10bn WSJ lawsuit, ruling he failed to prove actual malice in the newspaper’s reporting.
articles.body:
A federal judge has permanently dismissed United States President Donald Trump’s multibillion-dollar defamation lawsuit against media mogul Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal.

On Saturday, US District Judge Darrin Gayles concluded that the president had failed to establish the standard of “actual malice” required for defamation suits.

Under US law, a successful complaint must show that the defendant released a defamatory statement knowing it was false or with “reckless disregard” for its accuracy.

Gayles, however, said that Trump was “grasping at straws” with his $10bn case against The Wall Street Journal.

“The Amended Complaint falls short of pleading actual malice,” Gayles wrote.

“Indeed, the allegations regarding malice are conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent with the Article and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew or should have known that the statements in the Article were purportedly false.”

The judge went so far as to suggest that Trump’s legal team had attempted “to manufacture flaws with the investigation” published in The Wall Street Journal.

The case stemmed from coverage that linked Trump to the late disgraced financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

On July 17, 2025, The Wall Street Journal published an exclusive describing a sexually suggestive birthday note gifted to Epstein for his 50th birthday in 2003, as part of a book of congratulatory letters.

The letters were reportedly collected by disgraced British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell , who is serving a 20-year prison sentence for her involvement in Epstein’s sex-trafficking scheme.

The note attributed to Trump includes typed text framed by a hand-drawn outline of what appears to be a curvaceous woman. At the bottom, where her pelvic region might be, is Trump’s signature.

Trump vehemently denied responsibility for the text, the signature and the artwork. A copy of the birthday letter was later released through the House Oversight Committee.

The Wall Street Journal’s article came at a time when Trump’s second administration was facing intense scrutiny over whether it had withheld documents about Epstein’s alleged sex crimes, despite promises of transparency.

Critics had also raised questions about the nature of Trump and Epstein’s relationship. The two men appear to have socialised together, and Epstein was known to have surrounded himself with powerful figures from politics, academia and the business world.

In 2025, Trump said he ended his relationship with Epstein after the financier “stole” female employees from his Mar-a-Lago resort.

Epstein was convicted of soliciting a minor for sex in Florida in 2008, for which he served 13 months in jail. In 2019, he faced federal charges related to sex trafficking, but he was found dead in his New York City jail cell before he could be brought to trial. His death was later ruled a suicide.

Legal advocates say Epstein’s victims are estimated to number in the hundreds.

After the release of The Wall Street Journal report, Trump branded the newspaper’s coverage “false, malicious, and defamatory”.

His lawsuit, filed in the federal court in Miami on July 18, 2025, accused the paper and its reporters of having “knowingly and recklessly” published “numerous false, defamatory, and disparaging statements”.

The result, it alleged, was “overwhelming financial and reputational harm” to the president. Two journalists associated with The Wall Street Journal article were named among the defendants.

In April, Judge Gayles dismissed the defamation lawsuit, ruling that Trump had failed to prove the reporting was borne of “actual malice”.

But that initial ruling gave Trump the opportunity to refile his complaint, which he did in May.

The updated lawsuit claimed The Wall Street Journal had been reckless in not showing how reporters had received and verified the letter.

Saturday’s Miami ruling deals a final blow to Trump’s attempt to sue over the issue. Gayles’s decision dismisses the case “with prejudice”, which effectively blocks any future litigation on the matter.

Trump has other ongoing defamation cases against other media outlets, including the BBC and The New York Times.

articles.title: Dutch authorities rescue 38 people adrift in rubber boat
articles.summary: Migrant boats are rarely found in Dutch waters, and authorities are still trying to establish where this one came from.
articles.body:
Authorities in the Netherlands have rescued 38 people found adrift in a rubber boat off the Dutch coast, in one of the first such interceptions for the country.

Two of the people on board the dinghy when it was rescued are thought to be smugglers, while the rest are migrants, military police spokesperson Doron Wallin told The Associated Press news agency on Saturday.

“We don’t know where they came from – France, the Netherlands or Belgium – and we don’t know where the boat was heading,” Wallin said.

The boat was discovered drifting with no motor off the coast of the Netherlands’ Zeeland province, far southwest of Amsterdam. No one was wearing a life vest.

All 38 on the boat were men, 36 of whom were from Afghanistan, and two – the suspected smugglers – were from Sudan, according to the AFP news agency. The two Sudanese men have been arrested on suspicion of people smuggling.

It is not known where the boat was headed, but refugee and migrant crossings in small boats from France to the United Kingdom have become commonplace in recent years. It is unusual for boats to be discovered in Dutch waters, however.

“These are things you usually see in France and Belgium. We rarely see it here in the Netherlands before today,” Wallin said.

Dutch authorities will open an investigation into the case on Sunday.

articles.title: Head of In-N-Out burger chain addresses expansion to 3 more states
articles.summary: CEO Lynsi Snyder named Arkansas, Mississippi and Oklahoma as possible future In-N-Out Burger states while stressing the chain's cautious approach to growth.
articles.body: In-N-Out Burger CEO Lynsi Snyder has hinted at future expansions for the California-based fast-food chain, mentioning Arkansas, Mississippi and Oklahoma as three states that might welcome In-N-Out restaurants in the years to come. Snyder, whose grandparents Harry and Esther Snyder co-founded In-N-Out in 1948, sat down for an interview with television host Terry Crews. She spoke about the company’s hesitancy to grow too much or too quickly. Quality matters more than quantity, she said, when it comes to In-N-Out restaurants. IN-N-OUT'S POPULAR BURGER STYLE STARTED WITH A CUSTOMER REQUEST DECADES AGO "I just want to make sure that everything is right and that our In-N-Out family is strong, and we’re retaining all those values," Snyder said, touting the chain’s cleanliness, quality and friendly service. "If I ever felt like we were slipping or losing our way, growth would look a lot different," she added. In-N-Out takes food quality seriously, with all ingredients delivered fresh to each restaurant. "In fact, we don’t even own a microwave or freezer," the company says on its website. REGIONAL BURGER CHAINS ARE BEATING FAST-FOOD GIANTS IN ONE KEY MEASURE The burgers are made from fresh beef in the chain’s patty-making facilities in California and Texas.
